 The stock market could be headed for more turbulence. How one investor is preparing
 Published Thu, Nov 19 2026 2:12 PM EST Todd Gordon @ToddFGordon WATCH LIVE (See the video above for Todd's complete chart breakdown.) Normally I use this weekly column to walk through the individual stocks we're adding, holding or cutting in our portfolios at Inside Edge Capital. This week I'm stepping back to the big picture. That's where the risk is right now. Between the geopolitical noise, the domestic political drama, some genuinely strange ghost-in-the-machine stuff, and Nvidia's blowout quarter amid its leadership transition, the indexes are trading almost schizophrenically. And they're sitting right at the edge of key support. If that gives way, it could open up a fresh wave of selling. Yesterday we rebalanced our Tactical Alpha Growth portfolio for the fifth time since October. We've been in business for five years, and this is by far our most active six-week stretch. We cut net equity exposure from 92% to 70%, raised cash to 20% in T-bills, and added a 5% hedge with an inverse Nasdaq 100 ETF. Here are the exact sector changes we shared with our clients. Beyond the worries over massive AI buildout spending, we're watching interest rates that just won't quit. The outlook now calls for at least three more Fed hikes over the next four months. Zoom out to the longest trend, and the 10-year TIPS yield tracks the value-to-growth ratio. Real yields are at 2.87%, the high end of the last decade, and the value-to-growth ratio is pressing against the top of the range it's held all year. If that blue line breaks out, value could continue to outperform growth. That's an uncomfortable spot in the middle of the AI revolution, and yesterday's moves position us for it. Of course, our portfolios, and probably yours, are sitting on nice gains in semiconductors. Selling those and writing a big check to the IRS next year isn't very appealing. So instead of dumping winners, we hedged growth with a 5% position in PSQ, the ProShares Short QQQ. The QQQ chart below lays out the levels. The $655 zone is the line in the sand. Below it there's a little air pocket down to about $635, the area that capped the market in the fourth quarter of 2025 and again in the first quarter of 2026. If we test $635 and it can't hold, I plan to add to the PSQ hedge. That's not a prediction. It's just a hard look at where things stand right now. If the market pulls itself together and holds $655, I'll close the hedge quickly, figure out where leadership is coming from based on sector rotation, and put the cash back to work. If your head is spinning, you're not alone. That's the kind of market we're in, and for active managers, this is when the tough get going. Todd Gordon is the founder of Inside Edge Capital, LLC .
